title: Prognosticator's Peril
summary:
Prognosticator's Peril
Having been blessed with the consistent ability to turn a black, messy fluid into gold, refiners have enjoyed strong margins in recent times. Although the refined products market has exhibited remarkable price resilience, some refiners are rethinking their plans to expand their Midas touch. Congressional testimony given this week by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) underscored the reluctance of US refiners to commit to tentative expansion plans announced last year.

children.title: Million Barrels Per Day
children.summary: Refinery Utilization Before the hurricanes of 2005, the chart shows refinery utilizations around 90% and occasionally rates even hovering at 95%. Even with most of the hurricane damage now repaired, recent utilization rates have barely hit 90%.

children.title: Thinking Long-Term
children.summary: The confluence of many factors obstructs the view of future refinery profitability. Economic returns from expansion projects are conceptualized based on estimates of construction costs and expectations of refinery margins.

children.title: Total Potential Additions 1,072
children.summary: As ship owners and charterers well know, planning, evaluating and executing significant investments is a perilous task in any market. Commitment to a major refinery expansion in the current investment environment is hindered by a cacophony of commentary on high gasoline prices and the production of more alternative transportation fuels.
